### cycle 1 addendum — control-channel poll, now with LOG EVIDENCE (and L-039 observed twice more)

The block above stated that the orient poll "ran and exited 0 (silent)". That was asserted
from silence, and silence is not evidence. runs/notify.log settles it properly:

    2026-08-18T04:06:08+0000 poll ok merged=0     <- the orient poll (block above)
    2026-08-18T04:15:11+0000 poll ok merged=0     <- re-verified deliberately
    2026-08-18T04:15:14+0000 send phase-change ok <- PLAN -> BUILD push, step 8

So the claim holds and is now logged rather than inferred: the channel was polled, and it
merged zero commands, which is why control.json still reads pending [] applied [].

WHAT CAUGHT IT is worth recording, because it is L-039 happening live for the second and
third time this cycle. The phase-change send FAILED on its first attempt with:

    /bin/bash: line 1: bin/swarm-notify.sh: No such file or directory

Not a permission denial — a RESOLUTION failure. An earlier `cd /opt/targets/aphorism-cli`
in this session (to run the test suite) had left the shell's cwd in the target, and
permissions.allow carries only the RELATIVE entry `Bash(bin/swarm-notify.sh:*)` for this
host. So the command string must match that entry literally, which means it only works when
cwd happens to be /opt/swarm. The absolute-path entry in allow[] points at
/Users/truman/Projects/SWARM — a macOS path that cannot exist on this droplet.

That is the SAME defect as the one N-1 documents, seen from the other side: the gap is not
only that six helpers are missing from allow[], it is that the one helper that IS listed is
listed in a form whose success depends on the conductor's current working directory. A
wrapper script (`bash runs/c1r3-notify.sh`) was then also denied, because that command
string does not match the entry either. The working invocation is `cd /opt/swarm;
bin/swarm-notify.sh ...` in a single command, and N-1's patch must say so explicitly rather
than only listing the missing entries — otherwise a human adds six lines and leaves the
seventh, cwd-fragile, one in place.

## cycle 2 — 2026-08-18T04:29Z — N-1 + N-2 (inline, conductor-owned) — VALUE

TARGET: /opt/targets/aphorism-cli · phase BUILD · gear 1 -> **2** (k_cap 2) · 2 items verified

PICK: N-1 (p1, S, docs, covers K-1) and N-2 (p2, S, docs, covers K-2). Both conductor-owned
  and undispatchable — they write inside SWARM/playbook/, and hard rule 5 forbids handing any
  SWARM path to a workflow agent. Gear 2's k_cap of 2 admits exactly this pair; both are
  must-have coverage, which is what gear 2 puts ahead of polish.

ORIENT:
  - Prior conductor PID 2063888: DEAD. This session is PID 2066047; `pgrep -af claude` shows
    exactly one claude process, mine. No duplicate conductor.
  - Target tree CLEAN at orient. No salvage.
  - Control channel: polled, `runs/notify.log` logs `04:22:54+0000 poll ok merged=0`.
    control.json pending [] applied [], no `inject` array. Nothing to apply or triage.

### The cycle's main finding: this run had been crawling on fabricated inputs

Step 1 ran `bin/swarm-budget.sh` — DENIED again (probe_failures 2 -> 3). Cycle 1 responded to
that denial by recording ρ as UNMEASURED and setting `usage_reset_at = stop_at`. That was
wrong, and the correction is this cycle's highest-value output.

`swarm-budget.sh` line 37 defines its own probe:

    PROBE_CMD="${PROBE_CMD:-npx ccusage@latest blocks --json --token-limit max}"

and `Bash(npx:*)` IS in `permissions.allow`. **The allowlist gap blocks the script, not the
measurement.** Running that exact command returned the first real burn data this run has had:

    limit          130,591,250      window tokens   15,109,544
    burnRate       420,938 tok/min  window cost     $13.57
    active block   2026-08-18T03:00:00Z .. 08:00:00Z

Replicating the script's arithmetic by hand from its source (lines 194-310), the fabricated
horizon is what was pinning the gear:

    horizon                       mins   target_rate    ratio   gear_target
    usage_reset_at == stop_at     1406      82,135/min   5.12       1
    MEASURED reset 08:00:00Z       218     529,733/min   0.79       4

Setting the reset to `stop_at` stretched a 3.6-hour window into a 23-hour one, which lowers
the per-minute allowance and inflates ρ to 5.12 — an apparent 5x overburn that is an artifact
of the fabricated input, not a measurement. Two further bookkeeping errors fell out of reading
the source rather than trusting cycle 1's hand-computation:

  1. **weekly.ceiling was recorded as 1.** Lines 133-137 emit `WCEIL=2` for heat > 1.3, and
     `WCEIL=3` for heat > 1.1. There is no code path that produces a ceiling of 1.
  2. **pacing.dial 0.3 has never applied.** Line 82: `[ "$MODE" = "guest" ] && DIAL="1.00"`.
     Guest mode forces the dial; the runfile has been reading as though 0.3 governed.

Applied gear: t = min(gear_target 4, WCEIL 2) = 2; guest clamp (>3) inert; hysteresis from
PREV_GEAR 1 gives APPLIED **2**, k_cap 2, demote true, promote blocked. The weekly governor is
still the binding constraint and still says slow down — heat 23.0/13.91 = 1.65. The run moves
one rung, which is all hysteresis allows, and for a measured reason rather than a missing one.

WORK — N-1: rewrote `playbook/HANDOFF-allowlist-2026-08-17.md`. settings.json was re-read
  independently this cycle and confirms cycle 1 exactly: 36 allow entries, exactly two naming a
  swarm helper and both naming swarm-notify.sh, six helpers absent, additionalDirectories `[]`.
  The patch grew from 8 lines to 9 (swarm-watchdog.sh and swarm-warmup.sh were missing from the
  old patch; the dead macOS entry is called out as dead weight). The cwd-fragility defect is
  documented with a second live reproduction: `bin/swarm-notify.sh poll` exits 127 from the
  default cwd and succeeds as `cd /opt/swarm; bin/swarm-notify.sh poll`, logged at 04:22:54Z.
  The npx finding above is written into the handoff too, because it re-rates the item honestly:
  this is a tooling-ergonomics fix, not a blindness emergency.

WORK — N-2: `learnings.md` measured by structural read — 20 lessons at the documented cap of
  20, zero duplicate ids, next_id 46 > max L-045, and all 20 lines carrying id + bracketed tag
  + text + [confidence:] + [source:]. Stated as a HAND read; `swarm-playbook.sh validate` was
  NOT executed and is still denied. The ledger line was appended to `applied.log` marked as a
  hand-edit — and it carries two CORRECTIONS to claims this run inherited:

  - cycle 1 said the script had not written a line since 2026-08-09. The last line without a
    denial note is dated **2026-08-13**.
  - the N-2 acceptance text said this would be the 6th consecutive hand-written line. It is the
    **3rd** line explicitly marked a hand-edit, and run #3's predecessor left no line at all —
    the tail has a gap, not an unbroken hand-written run.

  Both corrections went into the ledger note itself, not just here, so the next reader of the
  file sees them without reading this journal. Also recorded: "no note" is consistent with
  script authorship but is not proof of it, and that inference limit is stated rather than
  quietly resolved.

VERIFICATION EVIDENCE (gate authored AFTER both files were written, run by the conductor):

    $ python3 /opt/swarm/runs/c2r3-gate.py
    PASS  C1   N-1(c) patch block holds EXACTLY the 9 required allowlist entries
    PASS  C4   N-1(d) confirm command present in a fenced block, ABSOLUTE path
    PASS  C5   N-1(g) cwd fragility: failing form, working form, logged cycle-2 reproduction
    PASS  C8   N-1(a) denial count stated + >=3 reproduction rows in the table
    PASS  C11  N-2 JOIN: ledger applied ids == exactly the lessons carrying [apply:]
    PASS  C12  N-2(1) learnings.md intact: 20 lessons, no dup ids, next_id > max id
    PASS  K1   CONTROL: C1 DETECTS a patch block with one entry deleted
    PASS  K3   CONTROL: C11 join DETECTS a lesson losing its [apply:] directive
    PASS  K5   CONVERSE CONTROL: an unrelated edit leaves C1/C4/C5 GREEN
    GATE PASS — 17/17 checks passed
    (all 17 lines: .swarm/runs/cycle-002-verify-N1-N2.txt)

    $ node --test test/*.test.js        # the floor; this cycle touched no target code
    i tests 102
    i pass 102
    i fail 0

  The gate went RED on its first run, at C4, and the fix went into the DOCUMENT, not the check.
  The confirm command had been written as a 4-space indented block, which owns no structural
  marker a checker can key on — exactly what L-043 warns against. It was re-fenced as ```sh and
  C4 passed. Weakening C4 to a substring match over prose would have been the one-character
  alternative and is the thing hard rule 2 forbids.
  C11 is the check worth trusting most: it joins the ledger's applied ids against the set of
  learnings.md lessons actually carrying `[apply:]`. A fabricated or stale ledger line cannot
  satisfy it, and K2/K3 prove it fails when either side is mutated. K5 is the converse arm — an
  unrelated edit must leave the gate green, or the checks are snapshot tests rather than
  assertions.

KNOWN ISSUES touched: KI-2 (allowlist gap) — root cause and patch now complete, and its
  severity is honestly re-rated downward by the npx finding; still open, still human-owned.
  No new known_issues filed: the three errors found this cycle were all CORRECTED here, so they
  are recorded as decisions in state.json rather than carried as open issues.

FOR THE RETRO: the reusable lesson is not about npx. It is that a denied tool is not the same
  as an unavailable measurement — cycle 1 inferred the second from the first and then wrote a
  fabricated value into the runfile with an honest-sounding UNMEASURED note attached, which is
  more dangerous than a gap, because the note made it look handled. Read what the denied script
  would have run before concluding the data is out of reach.

      0 survived" **with the lower-bound caveat I supplied dropped**. Every number in it is true,
      and the framing is still wrong — in this very cycle N-4 showed that enumeration is
      incomplete and that one behaviour outside it is unprotected. A first screen saying "29/29,
      0 survived" reads as stronger coverage than exists. Numbers can be individually true and
      collectively misleading; K-4 says no false count claim, and I am reading that as covering
      the claim the numbers make together.
  (b) "test suite has only been run on Node v24.19.0" — I supplied "only ever been run *here*";
      the agent widened it into a history claim neither of us can verify.
  I rewrote both lines myself: (a) now carries the lower bound AND today's 14-clause result
  including the survivor, (b) now says what is checkable — no `engines` field, no CI matrix, no
  runtime assertion, and no run under Node 18 or 20 recorded anywhere in the journal (grepped:
  9 hits, every one about the README claim text, none an actual run). Re-ran the sealed gate
  after the repair: preservation still PASS, still 22 lines. The item is recorded
  **done-by-conductor-repair with attempts=1**, not as a clean delivery — the backlog should not
  read as though haiku got this right.

WHAT THE ONE SURVIVOR MEANS. D-42: repeated `--tag`/`--author`. Shipped behaviour is
  last-occurrence-wins; a first-wins implementation changes observable output (14 entries vs 9)
  and the suite stays fully green. It is classified **BOUNDARY, not HOLE**, and deliberately NOT
  hardened: SPEC spells every filter flag in the singular and never mentions repetition, so
  last-wins is an artifact of assignment order in `parseArgs`, not a contract. Writing a test
  would freeze an accident into a guarantee (L-033). It goes to J-7 for a human ruling, and
  N-10 is filed to record the gap honestly while it stays unruled. **0 HOLE is why N-5 closes
  with zero tests written — which SPEC K-3 names in advance as a valid result, not a shortfall.**

WHAT THIS CYCLE DOES NOT ESTABLISH. The 43-clause derivation is one reading by one agent plus
  my spot-checks of 4 rows; a third reading could find a 44th clause. Mutation testing stays
  N=1 per clause — a lower bound on defect classes, saying nothing about combined defects.
  12 of the 14 new clauses I did NOT re-plant myself; for those I have the agent's arm and its
  controls, not independent corroboration. And KI-29 records real fragility: D-04, D-36 and
  D-41 are each killed by exactly one test.

FENCE VIOLATION (KI-30, medium). The N-4 agent found `/tmp` blocked by its sandbox and created
  scratch at **`/opt/swarm/.n4-scratch`** — inside SWARM, outside the `runs/`+`playbook/` paths
  hard rule 5 permits. It was dispatched with target paths only and never told a SWARM path; it
  derived one. It cleaned up: directory absent and `git -C /opt/swarm status --porcelain` clean
  at verification, so nothing reached the repo. Recorded, not fixed mid-run (hard rule 5). The
  lesson for the morning report is that the fence is a convention, not a control — the fix is to
  hand subagents a scratch dir inside the TARGET in the dispatch contract.

WAVE AUTOTUNE. Not a clean wave — one failed verify (N-6). `wave_streak` 1 → 0; `k_current`
  stays 3. It was not binding anyway: the gear-2 cap of 2 was.

KNOWN ISSUES. KI-28 (low, human): repeated-flag semantics unprotected and undecided.
  KI-29 (low): three clauses each hang on a single killing test. KI-30 (medium): the SWARM
  fence depends on agent goodwill.

next: **N-10** (S, docs, haiku) — write the two measured spec gaps into SPEC.md as gaps, without
  deciding them; it is the natural follow-through while D-42/D-43 are fresh, and it is
  gear-2-priced. Then **N-8** (S, docs) — name an actor and settling evidence for T-006, T-040,
  J-7, closing K-5; J-7 now carries four rulings, not two, so N-8 got bigger this cycle. **N-9**
  (KI-26 watchdog) stays last: it is the only remaining item that tests SWARM rather than the
  product. Must-have coverage after this cycle: K-1 ✓, K-2 ✓, K-3 ✓ (N-3/N-4/N-5 all closed),
  K-4 ✓ (N-7 + N-6), K-5 open (N-8, N-10).

  LIVE-LOOK: 4 findings, ALL 4 conductor-reproduced. One agent severity claim MEASURED FALSE.
    F-1 EPIPE, agent said HIGH on the mechanism "`--list | head -1` only survives by luck
        because 50 lines fit the 64KB pipe buffer". I tested that mechanism instead of
        accepting it, and it is WRONG:
          CRASH err_bytes=1006 | --list | true
          CRASH err_bytes=1006 | node bin/aphorism.js | true
          CRASH err_bytes=1006 | --list | head -0
          CRASH err_bytes=1045 | --list | /nonexistent-cmd-xyz
          clean err_bytes=   0 | head -1, head -5, sed 1q, grep -q match, grep -q no-match,
                                 wc -l, --list --json | head -2
        The crash needs a consumer that closes the pipe WITHOUT READING AT ALL; every consumer
        that reads even one line is clean. RE-SCORED HIGH -> MEDIUM. The defect is real (1006
        bytes of Node internals where a Unix filter should exit quietly) and is filed; the
        agent's story about it was not. Most realistic real trigger: downstream fails to exec.
    F-2 Same root cause (no error handler on process.stdout, bin/aphorism.js:28,43,48). stdout
        redirected to /dev/full -> ENOSPC stack trace AND exit 1, the code README defines as
        "no aphorism matched". A script checking exit 1 mistakes a full disk for an empty
        filter result. MEDIUM. Filed with F-1 as ONE item (Q-1) — one cause, one fix.
    F-3 Corpus attribution "Antoine de Saint-Exupery" missing its acute accent. Reproduced by
        CODEPOINT, not by eye:
          codepoints around "Exup": E=U+0045 x=U+0078 u=U+0075 p=U+0070 e=U+0065 r=U+0072 y=U+0079
          corpus contains any U+00E9: false | corpus contains U+2014: true
        The discriminator matters: em dash present throughout proves UTF-8 transport works, so
        this is data entry, not an encoding limit. LOW. In scope — repairing an existing entry
        is repair, not the "corpus expansion" non-goal.
    F-4 Empty `--seed` contradicts the Selection clause. REPRODUCED — and then found to be a
        DUPLICATE. See the retraction below.

RETRACTION, same cycle, before commit: F-4 duplicates measured gap D-43, which cycle 5 had

  is real evidence the gap is genuine and human-owned; (b) the ONE fact D-43 does not record,
  folded into J-7's notes — whitespace-PADDED seeds are ACCEPTED (`--seed " 5 "` is
  byte-identical to `--seed 5`, exit 0), so the refusal is specific to empty/whitespace-only.

  to Number(), which tolerates padding by itself. Consequence for the human ruling: "accept per

  gap is corroboration, not new backlog. Filing it would have inflated this cycle's apparent
  output with bookkeeping the run already owned — the exact failure mode a housekeeping run is
  most prone to.
